extracted.intended_audience: educated readers and policymakers interested in political theology and scriptural interpretation (clergymen, sovereigns, and learned public)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and normative criteria for reading Scripture and judging ecclesiastical rites and claims insofar as they bear on civil sovereignty, consecration, and doctrines about the soul and afterlife. Focuses on how to deduce lawful political and ecclesiastical consequences from Scripture without error or abuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpret scripture by scope and design, not isolated texts
rubrics_metrics.description: It is not the bare Words, but the Scope of the writer that giveth the true light, by which any writing is to bee interpreted; and they that insist upon single Texts, without considering the main Designe, can derive no thing from them cleerly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When arguing from Scripture prefer the author's overall purpose and harmony with the whole Bible; avoid deriving doctrines or political claims from single, decontextualized verses (described as 'casting atomes of Scripture').

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid obscure or controverted texts; allege plain, harmonious senses
rubrics_metrics.description: In the allegation of Scripture, I have endeavoured to avoid such Texts as are of obscure, or controverted Interpretation; and to alledge none, but is such sense as is most plain, and agreeable to the harmony and scope of the whole Bible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer clear, broadly harmonious passages when supporting doctrinal or political conclusions; treat obscure passages cautiously and not as the primary foundation for contentious claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Civil sovereign's laws and duties within Christian commonwealth
rubrics_metrics.description: There can therefore be no contradiction between the Laws of God, and the Laws of a Christian Common-wealth. Whosoever therefore obeyeth his Christian Soveraign, is not thereby hindred, neither from beleeving, nor from obeying God.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subjects should obey the lawful civil sovereign even where the sovereign's deductions or secondary practices may err; obedience to the civil sovereign does not prevent private belief and is required for public order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obedience to an infidel sovereign; private faith tolerated but resistance is sinful
rubrics_metrics.description: And when the Civill Soveraign is an Infidel, every one of his own Subjects that resisteth him, sinneth against the Laws of God ... Their Faith, it is internall, and invisible; They have the licence that Naaman had, and need not put themselves into danger for it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Private/internal profession of faith is permitted without public resistance; subjects must not make war upon an infidel sovereign nor use expectation of martyrdom as an excuse for disobedience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not equate the present Church with the Kingdom of God
rubrics_metrics.description: The greatest ... abuse of Scripture ... is the wresting of it, to prove that the Kingdome of God ... is the present Church ... Which second coming not yet being, the Kingdome of God is not yet come, and wee are not now under any other Kings by Pact, but our Civill Soveraigns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret references to the Kingdom of God historically and eschatologically (future/restored), not as justification for ecclesiastical temporal supremacy or for treating the present church as Christ's kingdom.

rubrics_metrics.name: Papal claims to vicarious universal authority are illegitimate for temporal power
rubrics_metrics.description: Consequent to this claim of the Pope to Vicar Generall of Christ ... is the Doctrine, that it is necessary for a Christian King, to receive his Crown by a Bishop ... That if a King ... doe not purge his Kingdome of Haeresies ... his Subjects are absolved of the bond of their obedience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reject doctrines and canonical claims (e.g., Lateran IV) that make papal or clerical rites the source or condition of lawful temporal sovereignty; historical context shows such claims grew with papal power rather than Scripture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consecration is dedication of use, not change of nature (avoid conjuration/transubstantiation)
rubrics_metrics.description: To Consecrate ... is to Offer, Give, or Dedicate ... thereby to change, not the thing Consecrated, but onely the use of it, from being Profane and common, to be Holy ... But when ... the nature of qualitie of the thing it selfe, is pretended to be changed, it is not Consecration, but either an extraordinary worke of God, or a vaine and impious Conjuration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat consecration as a change in use/signification (e.g., bread to signify Christ's body), not as producing a literal alteration of substance; literalist/transubstantiation claims are characterized as conjuration and idolatry with examples provided (bread/wine).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ceremonies must be decent, significant, and conformable to the action
rubrics_metrics.description: Those governors are obliged to such direction, as the nature of the action it selfe requireth; as that the ceremonies, words, and gestures, be both decent, and significant, or at least conformable to the action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ritual elements should be appropriate to the purpose (examples: Moses' simple anointing and prayer vs later exorcisms); innovations like exorcised water, repeated spittle, or irrelevant formulas are improper additions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid turning consecrations into incantations or exorcisms
rubrics_metrics.description: A second generall abuse of Scripture, is the turning of Consecration into Conjuration, or Enchantment ... when by such words, the nature of the thing it selfe, is pretended to be changed, it is ... a Conjuration or Incantation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use charms, repeated conjurations, or alleged magical formulas (e.g., extensive exorcisms in baptism, benediction of salt/oil) as if they effected physical/metaphysical changes; treat such practices as superstitious innovations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject pagan daemonology and phantasms as sources for Christian doctrine
rubrics_metrics.description: Secondly, by introducing the Daemonology of the Heathen Poets ... which are but Idols, or Phantasms of the braine ... Thirdly, by mixing with the Scripture divers reliques of the Religion, and much of the vain and erroneous Philosophy of the Greeks, especially of Aristotle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid incorporating heathen daemonology, mythic ghost lore, or questionable Greek philosophical remnants into Christian theology; these imports are named among the principal causes of 'spirituall darkness'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not found doctrines (purgatory, eternal torments, invocation of saints, indulgences) on obscure texts
rubrics_metrics.description: This window it is, that gives entrance to the Dark Doctrine, first, of Eternall Torments; and afterwards of Purgatory, and consequently of the walking abroad ... of the Ghosts of men deceased; and thereby to the pretences of Exorcisme and Conjuration of Phantasmes; as also of Invocation of men dead; and to the Doctrine of Indulgences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Difficult or obscure New Testament places should not be read as proving doctrines like purgatory or indulgences; the whole scope of Scripture should be considered and previously answered texts reviewed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpret ambiguous prophetic texts by grammar, context, and immediate narrative
rubrics_metrics.description: The words are (Mark 9.1.) 'Verily, I say unto you, that there be some of them that stand here, which shall not tast of death, till they have seene the Kingdome of God come with power.' ... If it be lawfull to conjecture at their meaning, by that which immediately followes, ... it is not unprobable, to say they have relation to the Transfiguration ... so that they saw Christ in Glory and Majestie, as he is to come; insomuch as 'They were sore afraid.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a passage is ambiguous (e.g., Mark 9.1), examine grammatical possibilities, the immediate narrative (e.g., Transfiguration), and analogies (e.g., other sayings about Peter and John) rather than assuming a universal doctrinal consequence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not use metaphorical or isolated verses to assert unjustified temporal papal supremacy
rubrics_metrics.description: As for some other texts, to prove the Popes Power over civill Soveraignes ... as that the two Swords ... were the Spirituall and the Temporall Sword ... One might as well inferre out of the first verse of the Bible, that by Heaven is meant the Pope, and by Earth the King.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid stretching metaphors or analogies (two swords, luminaries) into literal proofs that the Pope holds temporal dominion; such argumentation is judged 'not arguing from Scripture, but a wanton insulting over Princes.'

rubrics_metrics.name: The name 'clergy' and clerical revenues are historical, not necessarily jure divino
rubrics_metrics.description: For Clergy signifieth those, whose maintenance is that Revenue ... assigned to the tribe of Levi ... The Pope therefore, (pretending the present Church to be, as the Realme of Israel) claiming to himselfe and his subordinate Ministers, the like revenue ... the name of Clergy was sutable to that claime.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that distinctions like 'clergy' vs 'laity' and claims to tithes and exemptions have historical origins in Israelite practice and later papal claims; these should not be automatically accepted as divine rights without scrutiny.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat alleged ritual efficacies (enchanted oil/water, spittle) skeptically
rubrics_metrics.description: In Marriage, In Visitation Of The Sick, Of Consecrating Churches ... there is in them the use of Enchanted Oyle, and Water, with the abuse of the Crosse, and of the holy word ... as things of efficacy to drive away Phantasmes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Question rites that depend on supposed enchanted substances or repeated verbal formulas; prefer rites that have clear, decent symbolism and scriptural or historical warrant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpret references to soul and life in Scripture as compatible with mortality plus grace
rubrics_metrics.description: The Soule in Scripture, signifieth alwaies, either the Life, or the Living Creature; ... the Souls of the Faithfull, are not of their own Nature, but by Gods speciall Grace, to remaine in their bodies, from the Resurrection to all Eternity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reading texts about the soul and immortality (e.g., Ecclesiastes 12.7, Gen. 5.24), prefer readings that make immortality a result of God's grace and resurrection rather than an intrinsic, natural property of the soul applicable to all people.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess theological claims in their historical development and motives
rubrics_metrics.description: Nor did the Church of Rome ever establish this Transubstantiation, till the time of Innocent the third; which was not above 500 years agoe, when the Power of Popes was at the Highest, and the Darknesse of the time grown so great ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When doctrines or rites appear, trace their historical emergence and the political/contextual factors (e.g., papal power expansion) that may have influenced adoption rather than assuming they are immutable scriptural truths.
